review_type: Exploratory engineer review of cue capture frames and context stills; no independent instructor labels

findings.configuration: semantic, assumed manual 30 km/h, 224 ms simulated delay
findings.observation: At capture 29.68 s, a genuine oncoming car and a second large car-labelled road region coexist. At capture 47.32 s, the large car-labelled road/guardrail region has no visible car. Both produce an obstacle instruction. This reproduces prior F01/F02 without a guidance-quality fix.
findings.limitation: The trace does not identify the responsible actor/track; attribution remains incomplete.

findings.configuration: semantic, assumed manual 30 km/h, 224 ms simulated delay
findings.observation: At capture 1.8667 s, the retained car detection is across the concrete divider at the far left, while the app says Traffic ahead. Keep a safe gap. Same-direction relevance is not established. Reproduces prior F03.

findings.configuration: semantic, unknown speed and assumed manual 30 km/h, 224 ms simulated delay
findings.observation: Traffic, a motorcycle and overtaking cars are visible in capture/context frames. At 5.3 s a large car to the left and multiple cars ahead coexist. At 33.3 s a car overtakes on the right and moves ahead. Obstacle cues occur at both times, but actor-linked risk and useful timing are not demonstrated; do not count these as either proven hazard detections or proven false obstacles.
findings.limitation: Sparse context stills do not establish relative speed, collision risk or instructor-approved wording.

findings.observation: The same four cue times occupy 33.48% of the clip with unknown speed and 45.27% with assumed manual 30 km/h. Longer slowdown/conditional engine-struggle wording explains the difference. No real gear or RPM measurement is supplied.
findings.limitation: Computed scheduled clip occupancy, not physical audio or a measured driver-distraction effect.

findings.observation: At assumed manual 30 km/h and 224 ms delay, two ordinary cues occupy 97.7% of the ten-second clip. The second interrupts the first. This reproduces the high-occupancy concern from prior F06.
findings.limitation: Startup speech is completed before the video. Occupancy clips interrupted speech and speech past the video end.

findings.observation: At 224 ms fixed result delay, semantic evidence is available in 46.72% of decision ticks after the first 350 ms of video. Freshness-limited silence must be reported separately from no relevant road user. This is consistent with the limited freshness margin exposed by the first phone capture.
findings.limitation: A fixed-delay replay is not a measured Android active-session trace. Preserve the freshness gate; investigate cadence and capture-to-result age.
